[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Rectangle Area II** [LC 850 · Rectangle Area II](https://leetcode.com/problems/rectangle-area-ii/){difficulty="Hard"}

Cut the plane along every $x$ that appears in the input and along every $y$ that appears. You get a grid of $(2n-1) \times (2n-1)$ cells, and here is the one fact that makes the problem solvable: **each cell is either entirely inside some rectangle or entirely outside all of them.** A rectangle's boundary can never pass through the interior of a cell, because every possible boundary line was used as a cut. So the cell is *uniform* — it has a single coverage state and a single area $(x_{i+1} - x_i) \cdot (y_{j+1} - y_j)$, and a point test at its centre answers for the whole cell.

That is A6's two-dimensional compression promoted to the solver: instead of counting how many segments cover a point, we accumulate the area of each strip. And the union is not the sum of the rectangle areas — overlapping ground would be counted twice — so we must aggregate per cell, never per rectangle.

[Solved in full in @sec-coord-p5-area.]{.card-link}

:::
